title: Neighbours Clean the River
text:
Last spring, a group of residents in a small town noticed that the river running through their park had become polluted. Plastic bottles and old tyres were floating near the banks, and the water smelled unpleasant. Instead of waiting for the council to act, the residents organised a weekend clean-up and invited local schools to join them.

Within three months, more than two hundred volunteers had collected several tonnes of rubbish. The group also installed signs asking visitors to take their litter home. Although the work was tiring, many participants said that meeting their neighbours made the effort worthwhile.

questions.text: What did the residents notice about the river?
options: It had been moved to a new place.

questions.text: How many volunteers had helped within three months?
Why did the residents organise the clean-up themselves?
options: They did not want to wait for the council to act.
They were paid by the local government.
They wanted to start a new business.
They had moved away from the town.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the signs the group installed?
options: They were meant to change visitors' habits.
They were removed after one week.
They warned people about the depth of the river.

people who live in a particular place

paragraph_translations: Geçen ilkbahar, küçük bir kasabadaki bir grup sakin, parklarından geçen nehrin kirlendiğini fark etti. Kıyılara yakın yerlerde plastik şişeler ve eski lastikler yüzüyordu ve suyun kokusu rahatsız ediciydi. Belediyenin harekete geçmesini beklemek yerine sakinler hafta sonu bir temizlik organize etti ve yerel okulları da katılmaya davet etti.

Üç ay içinde iki yüzden fazla gönüllü birkaç ton çöp topladı. Grup ayrıca ziyaretçilerden çöplerini evlerine götürmelerini isteyen tabelalar da yerleştirdi. İş yorucu olmasına rağmen birçok katılımcı, komşularıyla tanışmanın bu çabaya değdiğini söyledi.
